record.paper_title: Open Problems in Constructive Function Theory
record.original_question: Does Sobolev orthogonality for monic Sobolev orthogonal polynomials admit a matrix Riemann-Hilbert characterization?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 4.1. Is there any matrix Riemann-Hilbert characterization of this kind of orthogonality?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mu_0,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_m$ be positive Borel measures on the real line with finite moments of all orders, and consider the Sobolev inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_S \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{m} \int_{\mathbb{R}} f^{(k)}(x)\,g^{(k)}(x)\,d\mu_k(x),$$
defined on the space of polynomials. For each non-negative integer $n$, let $P_n$ denote the unique monic polynomial of degree $n$ satisfying $\langle P_n,q\rangle_S = 0$ for every polynomial $q$ of degree strictly less than $n$ (i.e., the monic Sobolev orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$).

In analogy with the Fokas–Its–Kitaev characterization of standard orthogonal polynomials on the real line — where the monic orthogonal polynomial of degree $n$ associated with a weight $w$ appears as the $(1,1)$-entry of the unique $2\times 2$ matrix-valued function $Y(z)$ that is analytic in $\mathbb{C}\setminus\mathbb{R}$, has prescribed jump $Y_+(x)=Y_-(x)\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1 & w(x)\\ 0 & 1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)$ on $\mathbb{R}$, and behaves like $Y(z)=(I+O(1/z))\,\mathrm{diag}(z^n,z^{-n})$ as $z\to\infty$ — does there exist a matrix-valued Riemann–Hilbert problem (with explicit jump contour, jump matrices, and asymptotic normalization determined by the data $(\mu_0,\dots,\mu_m)$) whose unique solution encodes the monic Sobolev orthogonal polynomials $P_n$ in a designated entry?
artifact.status_search_result: For Sobolev inner products of the discrete/coherent-pair type and several specific Sobolev settings, matrix Riemann–Hilbert characterizations have been derived (e.g., by reformulating scalar Sobolev orthogonality as matrix orthogonality on the real line, after work of Fokas–Its–Kitaev and subsequent extensions by Cassatella-Contra, Mañas, Branquinho and others). However, a fully general matrix Riemann–Hilbert characterization for arbitrary continuous Sobolev inner products with several derivatives does not appear to be established in a uniform way, and the question is best described as partially answered rather than completely resolved.

status_evidence.title: Properties of Matrix Orthogonal Polynomials via their Riemann-Hilbert Characterization
status_evidence.snippet: Riemann–Hilbert analysis is used to obtain information about matrix orthogonal polynomials and functions of second kind associated with a weight matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Matrix RH characterizations exist for matrix orthogonal polynomials, providing the framework needed to address Sobolev cases via reduction.

status_evidence.title: Riemann–Hilbert problems, matrix orthogonal polynomials and discrete matrix equations with singularity confinement
status_evidence.snippet: Scalar orthogonal polynomials with a Sobolev inner product involving a finite number of derivatives can be studied using matrix orthogonal polynomials on the real line.
status_evidence.claim: Sobolev orthogonality with finitely many derivatives can be reduced to matrix orthogonality, yielding partial RH characterizations.
